newsitem.title: USA: Canadian domestic natgas rises on storage refills.
newsitem.headline: Canadian domestic natgas rises on storage refills.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices edged higher Monday in the domestic markets due to some early storage injections, market sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices for Tuesday climbed to about C$1.50-1.53 per gigajoule (GJ), up about six cents from Friday's levels.
One trader noted that about 309 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gas was injected into the AECO storage hub on Saturday.
Storage inventories in the West as of March 14 were at 50.10 bcf, or 19.33 percent full, according to Canadian Gas Association data. This compares with year-ago tallies at 27.4 percent.
In pursuit of the daily market, April AECO prices were at C$1.49-1.53 per GJ, while May prices firmed to about C$1.50-1.52, Calgary-based sources said.
At Sumas, Wash., swing prices were little changed around $1.15 per million British thermal units (mmBtu). April pricing was talked at $1.08-1.09, about even with March indices.
At Niagara, prices for Tuesday failed to budge from last Friday's $2.18-2.20 amid moderate weather forecasts.
